{{Short description|The isometry group of a Riemannian manifold is a Lie group}}
Two [[theorems]] in the [[mathematical]] field of [[Riemannian geometry]] bear the name '''Myers–Steenrod theorem''', both from a 1939 paper by [[Sumner Byron Myers|Myers]] and [[Norman Steenrod|Steenrod]].  The first states that every distance-preserving surjective map (that is, an [[isometry]] of [[metric space]]s) between two [[Connected space|connected]] [[Riemannian manifolds]] is a [[Smooth function|smooth]] [[Isometry (Riemannian geometry)|isometry]] of Riemannian manifolds.  A simpler proof was subsequently given by [[Richard Palais]] in 1957. The main difficulty lies in showing that a distance-preserving map, which is a priori only [[continuity (topology)|continuous]], is actually [[Differentiable function|differentiable]].

The second theorem, which is harder to prove, states that the [[isometry group]] <math display="inline">\mathrm{Isom}(M)</math> of a connected <math>\mathcal{C}^2</math> Riemannian manifold <math display="inline">M</math> is a [[Lie group]] in a way that is compatible with the [[compact-open topology]] and such that the action <math display="inline">\mathrm{Isom}(M)\times M \longrightarrow M</math> is <math display="inline">\mathcal{C}^1</math>differentiable (in both variables). This is a generalization of the easier, similar statement when <math display="inline">M</math> is a [[Riemannian symmetric space]]: for instance, the group of isometries of the two-dimensional unit [[sphere]] is the [[orthogonal group]] <math display="inline">O(3)</math>. A harder generalization is given by the Bochner-Montgomery theorem, where <math display="inline">\mathrm{Isom}(M)</math> is replaced by a locally compact transformation group of diffeomorphisms of <math display="inline">M</math>.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bochner |first1=Salomon |last2=Montgomery |first2=Deane |date=1946 |title=Locally Compact Groups of Differentiable Transformations |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1969226 |journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume=47 |issue=4 |pages=639–653 |doi=10.2307/1969226 |jstor=1969226 |issn=0003-486X|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
